narrative.overview:
The site is a cool grey workbench on which small, real objects from Mathieu's life are laid out: a bio, what he is doing now, the book he is reading, the latest essay, a trip, the work. Each object is a flat tile and each tile is a door. Recognisable with the content removed: a grey field, flat near-white rectangles of varied size, mono caps labels, one orange dot. Geist does all the talking; Geist Mono labels and counts.

The system is flat on purpose. Tiles are separated by space and a 1px hairline, never by shadow, glass or gradient. Orange is a signal for state (playing, current, latest, pressed, focus), not decoration. The only dark, textured, lit object on the bench is the 3D living room. Everything else is paper and graphite.

The essay breaks no rule of the bench; it only removes the bench. Reading pages are a single plain column, no banner, no sidebar, no cards.
keyCharacteristics: Flat tiles on a grey field: 1px hairline, no drop shadow, no glass, no blur.
One family (Geist) plus its mono (Geist Mono) for labels, data and code.
Orange only for state; `--accent-graphic` for small marks (dots, underlines), `--accent` for fills.
Light and dark are both first-class; a tile can locally invert without any prop on its atoms.
Photos are ordered-dither duotones that reveal true colour on hover, focus or tap.
The room is the one dark object, painted with its own art-direction colours that never change with the theme.

rules.name: The Orange Is State Rule
rules.body: Orange means playing, current, latest, pressed or focused. If removing it loses no meaning, it should not be there.

rules.name: The Small Marks Rule
rules.body: Dots and underlines use `--accent-graphic`; fills use `--accent`. Never paint a small orange mark with `--accent` on paper.

rules.name: The Fixed Scrim Rule
rules.body: Text over a photo uses `--scrim` and `--scrim-foreground`, which do not change with the theme.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Geist for everything, Geist Mono for labels, data and code. No second display face, no serif.

rules.name: The Semantic Size Rule
rules.body: Components use the `--text-*` roles, never raw `--font-size-*` or literal sizes.

rules.name: The Bench Grid Rule
rules.body: Tiles are placed with `span`, `rows` and `order`; pages never write their own grid for a bench.

rules.name: The Plain Reading Rule
rules.body: The essay is one column. Apparatus (In short, back links) is orientation, never the only path.

rules.name: The No Shadow Rule
rules.body: No drop shadows, glass or blur on the bench or in the reading pages. The room's bookshelf carries its own painted shadows as part of the lit scene; that is the room's material, not a rule for the interface.

dos: **Do** separate tiles with space and a 1px `--border` hairline.
**Do** write atoms against the paper semantic names so they retint on any inverse surface.
**Do** use `--accent-graphic` for dots and underlines, `--accent` for fills, and only for state.
**Do** use `Bench`, `Tile`, `Page` and `PageTitle` for layout; add a variant before adding a component.
**Do** keep every target 44px and keep light and dark identical in structure.
**Do** keep the essay a single justified, hyphenated 38rem column opening with In short.
donts: **Don't** add drop shadows, glass, blur or gradients to tiles, controls or pages (the lit room scene is the exception, inside the room).
**Don't** use orange as decoration or for large areas outside primary buttons and pressed toggles.
**Don't** introduce a second typeface or colour literals outside `tokens.css` and `theme.css`.
**Don't** nest links or buttons inside a linked `Tile`.
**Don't** swap `--surface` and `--surface-inverse` inside the inverse rule.
**Don't** add a banner, sidebar or card to the essay.
